title: Extended Equipment Warranty Plans — Claim Service Standards, Maintenance Conditions and Exclusions by Tier
content:
Conditions of the Extended Equipment Warranty Plans concerning the timing of a claim, the maintenance the owner must keep, the service standard on an approved part and the exclusions. The figures below are those of the tier the plan is written at.

## 1. Time limits and thresholds

| Tier | Claim must be filed within (from the day the fault is found) | Claim adjudicated within (from filing) | Repair value above which authorisation is required before work starts | Approved part shipped within | Fee to expedite an approved part | Appeal must be lodged within (from denial) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Manufacturer Warranty Registration | 30 calendar days | 15 business days | 0 USD | 10 business days | 0 USD | 30 calendar days |
| Parts Protection Plan | 30 calendar days | 10 business days | 500 USD | 7 business days | 185 USD | 30 calendar days |
| Parts & Labor Protection Plan | 30 calendar days | 10 business days | 750 USD | 5 business days | 165 USD | 30 calendar days |
| Compressor Coverage Plan | 21 calendar days | 7 business days | 1000 USD | 5 business days | 145 USD | 30 calendar days |
| Major Component Protection Plan | 21 calendar days | 5 business days | 1500 USD | 3 business days | 125 USD | 45 calendar days |
| Total Equipment Protection Plan | 14 calendar days | 3 business days | 2500 USD | 2 business days | 0 USD | 45 calendar days |

## 2. Maintenance conditions

| Tier | Active maintenance agreement at the site required to keep the cover | Last documented maintenance visit must fall within (before the fault) |
|---|---|---|
| Manufacturer Warranty Registration | Not required | 12 calendar months |
| Parts Protection Plan | Not required | 12 calendar months |
| Parts & Labor Protection Plan | Required | 12 calendar months |
| Compressor Coverage Plan | Required | 9 calendar months |
| Major Component Protection Plan | Required | 6 calendar months |
| Total Equipment Protection Plan | Required | 6 calendar months |

The proof-of-maintenance period is the number of calendar months within which the last documented maintenance visit on the unit must fall for a claim to be paid. It is a condition of every tier, including the two that do not require a maintenance agreement.

## 3. Exclusions

On every tier of the Extended Equipment Warranty Plans:

- faults present before enrollment (pre-existing conditions) are excluded;
- damage from misuse, flood, fire or power events (abuse and misuse) is excluded.

Both exclusions apply on all six tiers; no tier of the plans is written without them.

## Points of judgement on the figures

- The Manufacturer Warranty Registration's authorisation threshold is 0 USD, and its expediting fee is 0 USD; the Total Equipment Protection Plan's expediting fee is likewise 0 USD while its authorisation threshold is 2500 USD.
- The filing period is counted in calendar days and the adjudication and shipping periods in business days; the two are never interchanged.
- The appeal period is 30 calendar days on the four lower tiers and 45 calendar days on the Major Component Protection Plan and the Total Equipment Protection Plan.
